groups.label: Harmony, Virtue, and Civic Role
groups.summary: Socrates examines the balance of civic and psychological constitutions, arguing that education and specialization must aim at the harmonious health of the entire soul and state. Virtue is presented as an internal alignment where reason directs the spirited and appetitive elements, mirroring the proportional order required of citizens.
groups.rationale: Gathers early-to-mid dialogue discussions focused on internal and civic harmony, functional justice, and soul health.

groups.label: Philosopher's Nature and State
groups.summary: Socrates delineates the attributes of the true philosopher and analyzes why exceptional minds become alienated or corrupted in prevailing societies. He proposes an appropriate educational progression, envisions public reconciliation with genuine wisdom, and mandates that enlightened thinkers return to govern the commonwealth.
groups.rationale: Unifies consecutive passages across Books VI and VII addressing the character of philosophers, their corruption by society, education, and civic obligation to rule.

groups.label: Dialectic as Supreme Science
groups.summary: Dialectic is contrasted with subordinate sciences and arts that depend on unexamined assumptions. It is characterized as the ultimate discipline that dispenses with hypotheses to reach direct apprehension of the good through pure reason.
groups.rationale: Binds the two occurrences that specifically define dialectic and contrast its first-principle inquiry with the hypothetical arts.

groups.label: Critique of Imitative Poetry
groups.summary: Socrates details the case against imitative arts, arguing that poets produce deceptive copies remote from truth and stimulate the inferior, emotive faculties of the soul. Poetry is excluded from the ideal commonwealth unless its advocates can demonstrate that it serves moral and political virtue.
groups.rationale: Covers the closely clustered sequence in Book X analyzing mimetic poetry, its psychological detriment, and the ancient quarrel with philosophy.
